sense.text:
“Remember this day, in which ye came out from Egypt, out of the house of bondage; for by strength of hand the Lord brought you out from this place.” By strength of hand: the Most High wasn’t playing. He flexed his strength, he flexed his power, when he was delivering us out of Egypt.

And when he brought us out he said, “there shall no leavened bread be eaten.” No bread with leaven. That is why we are celebrating the days of unleavened bread.

Some say, we don’t eat leaven for seven days, that’s just weird. But everything we celebrate has a meaning behind it. The Lord didn’t tell us to kill a lamb for no reason, or to keep tabernacles, or to eat no bread with leaven for no reason. He has his reasons behind these things, and the scriptures show them.

“Seven days thou shalt eat unleavened bread, and in the seventh day shall be a feast to the Lord.” Seven days we have to eat unleavened bread.

“There shall no leavened bread be seen with thee, neither shall there be leaven seen with thee in all thy quarters.” No leaven should be seen with you, and in all your quarters there should be no leaven.

“And thou shalt shew thy son in that day, saying, This is done because of that which the Lord did unto me when I came forth out of Egypt.” This verse explains why we celebrate unleavened bread. “This is done”: the feast of unleavened bread is done.

What did the Lord do unto them when they came out of Egypt? He delivered everyone, yes, but did everyone enter the promised land? No. The Lord purged everybody. In the wilderness he killed every rebel twenty years old and upward, everyone that had leaven in them.

So who is the “me” here? It is not Moses, and it is more than just Israel the nation. It is the ones that were children in the wilderness, under twenty, who made it into the land. The Lord purged the leaven out of him in the wilderness; all the adults did not make it, but he made it. Now he is grown, he is in the land, and he is telling his son why we keep the feast of unleavened bread: we keep it because the Lord did this to me. He got all the leaven out of me in the wilderness. There are levels to this.

“And it shall be for a sign unto thee upon thine hand, and for a memorial between thine eyes”: something you can see. “That the Lord’s law may be in thy mouth.”

That is why we keep the days of unleavened bread: it is a sign for us to keep God’s laws and remember God’s laws, for them to be in our mouths and in our minds. That is what the days of unleavened bread really represent. “For with a strong hand hath the Lord brought thee out of Egypt.”
“Thou shalt therefore keep this ordinance in his season from year to year.” This is the days of unleavened bread, kept every year: the days when the Lord got the leaven out of us in the wilderness.

precepts.why:
“How long shall I bear with this evil congregation, which murmur against me?” When we came out of Egypt our people were evil. We were taught they were righteous, but they were rebellious: a bunch of liars, fornicators and murmurers.

“As truly as I live, saith the Lord, as ye have spoken in mine ears, so will I do to you: Your carcases shall fall in this wilderness.” I’m going to kill all of you. This is what the Lord did unto us when he brought us out of Egypt. “All that were numbered of you, according to your whole number, from twenty years old and upward”: once you were twenty and up, the Lord said, I’m killing you.

Aaron died too. And the Lord killed Moses. Moses was not evil, but the people provoked Moses to anger, and the Lord told him he would not see the promised land. Moses understood that when he left his body he was going back to paradise.

“Doubtless ye shall not come into the land, concerning which I sware to make you dwell therein, save Caleb the son of Jephunneh, and Joshua the son of Nun.” Joshua and Caleb were the only two adults the Lord allowed to live and make it into the promised land. Everyone else twenty and up was killed.

According to the law, twenty and up is the age of a man: you take responsibility for yourself. That is why brothers and sisters are told twenty is the time they can marry; you should be responsible enough at that age. Back then everybody twenty and up had their blood on their own head, and God killed all of them.

“But your little ones, which ye said should be a prey, them will I bring in, and they shall know the land which ye have despised.” The little ones are the ones who later told their children, God did this to us in the wilderness. Everybody twenty and up was killed because they were evil, because they had leaven in them.

“And your children shall wander in the wilderness forty years, and bear your whoredoms, until your carcases be wasted in the wilderness.” The children saw all the evil the adults were doing, until every last one of those wicked Israelites died: “each day for a year, shall ye bear your iniquities, even forty years.”

So in those forty years in the wilderness the Lord killed all the rebellious: everybody murmuring, the adulterers who held on to Egypt, everyone among us that had leaven in them. The Lord purged that leaven out of our people. That is what the son is told in Exodus 13:8, and that is why we keep the feast.

sense.text:
“Seven days shall ye eat unleavened bread; even the first day ye shall put away leaven out of your houses: for whosoever eateth leavened bread from the first day until the seventh day, that soul shall be cut off from Israel.” Pay attention when you read: that soul.

Whoever eats leaven, or keeps leaven in their habitation, within those seven days, that soul is cut off. That is not talking about just regular death. Your soul being cut off is your name being blotted out of the book of life. That is damnation, condemnation.

So the leaven here is not just bread with yeast in it. It is something much more symbolic.

precepts.why:
“And offer a sacrifice of thanksgiving with leaven”: with sin. We thought that was acceptable to God. You cannot be in the midst of sin and give God thank offerings. The Lord says, I don’t work with that, I don’t deal with that.

“For this liketh you, O ye children of Israel.” That is how you black people is: in the midst of sin and coming to God with offerings. The leaven is sin.

“Take heed and beware of the leaven of the Pharisees.” The leaven of the Pharisees was hypocrisy; the leaven of the Pharisees is sin. Christ is saying, be careful of the sins of the Pharisees, who say and do not.

So the leaven is really sins. When the scriptures say we are not to eat leaven, being without leaven seven days is us being without sin. The days of unleavened bread we are keeping right now represent that. If anyone has leaven in them for those seven days, their soul will be cut off. It goes into something much heavier.

“And after seven days the world, that yet awaketh not, shall be raised up”: that is us being raised up and getting the kingdom. When will that happen? After seven days.

Within those seven days we are in the midst of sin, in the midst of all wickedness. But there will be a group of us that get rid of the leaven inside of us, that are unleavened within those seven days, and their soul will not be cut off. Everyone that took part in leaven, that has leaven in their heart, their soul will be destroyed when the Lord returns.

“And that shall die that is corrupt.” That is what Exodus says: within the seven days, whoever eats leaven, that soul is cut off. Taking part in leaven means you are corrupt.

“And the earth shall restore those that are asleep in her”: everybody coming back, the righteous coming back, after seven days.

So the seven days of unleavened bread is us getting ourselves together right now: fighting and not taking part in the leaven, fixing ourselves, becoming better people. You know the sins you are battling; get rid of them. Because when the Lord returns and we have not gotten rid of the leaven, the soul is cut off.

It is the same as when we came out of Egypt. In the wilderness the Lord purged the leaven out of us, and the same thing will happen again in the future.

sense.text: “All our fathers were under the cloud, and all passed through the sea; And were all baptized unto Moses in the cloud and in the sea.” Being baptized unto Moses means Moses taught us the laws.

“They drank of that spiritual Rock that followed them: and that Rock was Christ.” It was Christ following us. That Yahawah that was in the wilderness with us was Christ, speaking on the behalf of the Father.

“But with many of them God was not well pleased: for they were overthrown in the wilderness.” God was not pleased with our people. He killed everyone twenty years old and up, and only the children were allowed into the promised land.

“Now these things were our examples, to the intent we should not lust after evil things, as they also lusted.” What happened to our forefathers in the wilderness is an example for us not to be like them. They were murmuring, fornicating, trying to overthrow Moses. Read it and say, I can’t do that; I have to train myself not to be like that.

“Neither be ye idolaters, as were some of them”: some of them were idol worshipers.

Why is Paul giving this example? Because we will be going back into the wilderness again.

“And I will bring you into the wilderness of the people.” This is a prophecy. After the second Exodus, after the Lord delivers us from this new Egypt, he is taking us back into the wilderness. That is why Paul said not to be like our fathers.

“And there will I plead with you face to face”: the same way he pleaded with us in the wilderness the first time.

“Like as I pleaded with your fathers in the wilderness of the land of Egypt, so will I plead with you.” He will do it again in this second Exodus, when we are delivered from America.

The Lord is going to say: sisters, stop wearing those damn weaves. Stop saying Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday. A lot of what we follow and do here in America is wrong, and every custom, every thought, everything learned here has to go. The Lord will teach us everything the right way, and show us the parts we were missing. We understood how the sun and the moon work hand in hand for the year, with some years having an extra month, but that wisdom was lost through slavery. We do our best by the moon to tell the feast days, but the sun and the moon were both for times and seasons.

And how did the Lord plead with us in the wilderness? He got rid of all the leaven: he killed everybody twenty years old and up. The same thing is going to happen again. A lot of us might make it out of Babylon and still not make it into the promised land.

“And I will cause you to pass under the rod”: the rod is correction. “And I will bring you into the bond of the covenant.” That is us being purged in the wilderness again, the same way he purged us before and got rid of the leaven from among us.

“And I will purge out from among you the rebels, and them that transgress against me.” The rebels are those that break God’s laws, those that have leaven in them.

“I will bring them forth out of the country where they sojourn, and they shall not enter into the land of Israel.” You are going to be delivered, caught up in the chariots, delivered out of that destruction, and still not enter into the land. Just as everyone was delivered from Egypt and not everybody made it into the promised land, there will be groups delivered that will not make it into the land. “And ye shall know that I am the Lord.”

precepts.why:
The bond of the covenant is in Hebrews. “For this is the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel after those days, saith the Lord”: after those days means after we are delivered out of here.

“I will put my laws into their mind, and write them in their hearts: and I will be to them a God.” We are going to know God’s laws and we will keep God’s laws. Today a brother gets up for work in his routine, walks into the donut store, eats the donut, and then remembers, damn, it’s the days of unleavened bread, how could I forget? But the Lord God says his laws will be in our minds. We will not forget, and we will do it, and we will serve him. That is the new covenant. We are in the beginning of it, and once Christ returns it will be fully established in the wilderness.

“And they shall not teach every man his neighbour, and every man his brother, saying, Know the Lord: for all shall know me, from the least to the greatest.” Nobody will have to go and teach anybody, because the Lord is going to teach us. All of us will know the Lord, from the least among us to the greatest.

So being brought into the bond of the covenant is being purged in the wilderness and coming out with God’s laws written in us.

sense.text: “The wilderness and the solitary place shall be glad for them”: glad for us. When we are delivered, the deserts in our land, Lebanon and those places, shall rejoice. “And blossom as the rose”: trees are going to start springing up over there.

“It shall blossom abundantly, and rejoice even with joy and singing.” We are connected to the earth. When the righteous people start ruling, everything changes: trees growing, the animals free. The creatures understand us. That may sound like Christianity, but the donkey did talk to Balaam.

“The glory of Lebanon shall be given unto it”: Lebanon is going to be beautiful. “They shall see the glory of the Lord, and the excellency of our God.” The majesty of the Lord: the Lord will be on the earth. That is why everything will change.

“Strengthen ye the weak hands, and confirm the feeble knees.” Those with feeble knees, the scripture says to confirm you, to tell you everything is going to be all right. “Say to them that are of a fearful heart”: those afraid of what they see coming, or afraid in this truth. “Be strong, fear not.”

“Behold, your God will come with vengeance.” God is going to come and destroy the white man. It has to be said plain, because some say it means vengeance on a spiritual demon Satan. No: he is talking about the white man, the Arabs, the Chinese, the people that destroyed his people.

There will be no reparations, and we don’t want any damn reparations. To hell with your reparations. What can they give us to repay the rape and murder done to us? Nothing. We want the Lord’s will. We want vengeance, payback. Some don’t like that kind of talk, but that is why Christ is coming back to judge the nations.

“Even God with a recompence”: even God with a payback. “He will come and save you.” Our job is to exhort the ones that are afraid and weak, that the Lord is coming with vengeance.

“Then the eyes of the blind shall be opened”: the Lord is going to open your eyes so you can see clear; he is going to teach you things. “And the ears of the deaf shall be unstopped”: everybody will hear, nobody hard-headed anymore.

“Then shall the lame man leap as an hart”: those whose legs are messed up, walking with a cane, will start leaping. “For in the wilderness shall waters break out, and streams in the desert.” In the wilderness: that is where this goes, back to the wilderness of Ezekiel 20.
“And the parched ground shall become a pool, and the thirsty land springs of water.” Springs of water are going to come up all over those desert places.

“And an highway shall be there, and a way, and it shall be called The way of holiness; the unclean shall not pass over it.” This is in the wilderness: the unclean are not going to pass over it, meaning they will not go into the land.

“But it shall be for those”: for the brothers and sisters that kept the commandments, that got rid of the leaven from inside of them.

“But the redeemed shall walk there”: the redeemed of Israel walking back into our land. “And the ransomed of the Lord shall return, and come to Zion with songs and everlasting joy upon their heads.” Those the Lord ransomed shall return to our land with songs and everlasting joy.

precepts.why:
“Worthy is the Lamb that was slain to receive power, and riches, and wisdom, and strength, and honour, and glory, and blessing.” Christ receives all these things.

“And every creature which is in heaven”: there are creatures in heaven, the angels. “And on the earth”: creatures created on the earth, the animals. “And under the earth”: that just means in the earth, worms and creatures that live deep in the earth that nobody has ever seen. “And such as are in the sea”: Leviathan, creatures in the sea no human being has ever seen, that the Lord created. “And all that are in them.”

“Heard I saying, Blessing, and honour, and glory, and power, be unto him that sitteth upon the throne.” They heard, and they understood. All the creatures understood. That is why the creatures understand us, and why the land and everything in it rejoices when the righteous rule.

sense.text:
“It is reported commonly that there is fornication among you.” Fornication is sexual sins. “That one should have his father’s wife”: this man was banging his father’s wife.

Under the law of marriage, a woman betrothed is that man’s wife, as Mary was betrothed to Joseph, even if the betrothal lasts five, ten or fifteen years. It may have been a sister betrothed to the brother’s father, and the brother slept with her. A man in his right mind is not going to sleep with his own mother; that was not his mother, but a woman promised to his father. Even so, it was such evil that it was “not so much as named among the Gentiles.”

“And ye are puffed up, and have not rather mourned, that he that hath done this deed might be taken away from among you.” They were puffed up and did not mourn. They should have put this brother away from among them.

“To deliver such an one unto Satan.” How do you deliver someone to Satan? You kick them out of the school: you can’t be among us anymore. Satan, you can have him; he ain’t right. That is only for those who will not repent and are not trying to change. Paul was pissed when he first heard what the brother did, but when the brother repented, Paul forgave him: if you forgive him, I forgive him too; we can’t be ignorant of Satan’s devices. That is a lesson for us too.

“For the destruction of the flesh, that the spirit may be saved in the day of the Lord Jesus.” You want to destroy that spirit of adultery. If one brother is allowed to commit adultery with no recompense, everybody starts. Deal with it. Don’t allow fornication to fester.

“Your glorying is not good. Know ye not that a little leaven leaveneth the whole lump?” The leaven there was fornication. Allow a little bit of fornication in the schools and it is going to spread. Those in the midst of sin cannot be left among us; you have to change.

Don’t fear men; fear what God can do to you. There are diseases out there. Some of you brothers, your rod could fall off. Some of these sisters, your vagina could start rotting, smelling like rotten fish. The Deacon’s own little sister died at twenty, HIV positive, and his stepmother died too; he has seen what can happen, and that is why there are things he does not play with. Keep poking here and poking there, and poke the wrong place, and now you are mourning and crying. Some among us right now have the monster. Brothers and sisters, stop playing around, and you young horny sisters too, don’t be stupid. There is a God.

“Purge out therefore the old leaven”: get rid of the sin. Everyone deals with different levels of sin, but it is your job to see what you are dealing with and work on getting rid of it, because after those seven days, if you haven’t gotten rid of it, your soul will be cut off.

“That ye may be a new lump, as ye are unleavened.” We are supposed to be unleavened, without sin. Are we without sin? No; whoever says, I’m perfect, is fake and phony as hell. Paul said we die daily: when you make a mistake you go to the Lord, forgive me, have mercy upon me, and you start over, and so you are without sin. Sin is always there in the mind and Satan is always there; it becomes a problem when you act on it.

“For even Christ our passover is sacrificed for us”: he was sacrificed for us, for us to repent of our sins.

“Therefore let us keep the feast, not with old leaven”: not with the old sins. We are in the feast of unleavened bread and we want to be unleavened. “Neither with the leaven of malice”: malice goes into hatred. “And wickedness.” These things are leaven; we shouldn’t have them in us.

“But with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth.” Ask yourself: am I really sincere in this truth, really trying to do what’s right? That is what the Lord looks for: people that are sincere and really trying to change. When you make a mistake you run to him quick, Lord, forgive me, I’m sorry, I ain’t going to do it again. You are sincere and not fake.

Some brothers and sisters are not here in sincerity and truth. Learn to pick up on the fake ones: they don’t love their brothers, their sisters or the Lord; they complain, they gossip, they murmur. That is all the people that were killed in the wilderness.

To be sincere is to believe it: Christ is a black man, and Christ is coming back with vengeance. Don’t lose faith; we are the people of this book. The whole world, the US government and all the governments, is pushing lies, and it is a small remnant pushing the truth. The odds are against us, and that makes it all the sweeter, all the more marvelous, when the Lord does his thing.

And from malice comes the root of bitterness. The two greatest things that destroy people in this truth are lust and bitterness. Many fall into fornication and go back into the world; and many brothers and sisters have left the truth because of bitterness, which is very hard to recover from.
Cain was the first to develop bitterness; bitterness began here, in the beginning. “Abel was a keeper of sheep, but Cain was a tiller of the ground.”

“And the Lord had respect unto Abel and to his offering: But unto Cain and to his offering he had not respect.” God respected Abel’s offering because Abel did what he was told to do. Cain wanted to do his own thing.

“And Cain was very wroth”: he was angry. That is where the bitterness starts. The anger came from jealousy: why accept his offering and not mine? The root of bitterness starts with anger, and anger, jealousy and malice go hand in hand; they all fall under the umbrella of hatred. Thou shalt not hate thy brother.

“And his countenance fell.” His face fell, it changed, the way dudes beast up their face. He was angry because his sacrifice was not accepted. And when his countenance fell, that is when Satan attacked him.

“And the Lord said unto Cain, Why art thou wroth? and why is thy countenance fallen?” The Lord saw it.

“If thou doest well, shalt thou not be accepted?” If you do what I tell you to do, I will accept you the same way I accept your brother.

“And if thou doest not well, sin lieth at the door. And unto thee shall be his desire, and thou shalt rule over him.” Ask yourself what Satan was doing there. Moses was being shown what took place, and Satan was there, working on Cain. When Cain got angry and his countenance fell, Satan was messing with him, and the Lord told him: fight Satan and do what’s right, otherwise Satan will rule you and control you. Whoever sins becomes his servant.

Satan was whispering all kinds of things in Cain’s head about his brother: I don’t like Abel, he acts all perfect, he’s full of it. And Cain ended up rising up and killing his brother. Satan was behind all of it. That is the beginning of the root of bitterness.

precepts.why:
“From that time forth began Jesus to shew unto his disciples, how that he must go unto Jerusalem, and suffer many things of the elders and chief priests and scribes, and be killed, and be raised again the third day.” Christ is telling the disciples he has to die and rise again to redeem the nation of Israel. That was a good thing. It is hard to understand, the same way it is hard to hear that some of us will be killed for teaching this truth. But it is a good thing: our fellow servants have to be killed the same way those before them were killed, and that has to be fulfilled.

Peter looked at it as a bad thing: “Then Peter took him, and began to rebuke him, saying, Be it far from thee, Lord: this shall not be unto thee.” No, Lord, I love you, why do you want to die? But Christ had already explained that he had to die to redeem the nation and bring the kingdom.

“But he turned, and said unto Peter, Get thee behind me, Satan: thou art an offence unto me.” Peter was possessed in that moment. Satan jumped on Peter; it was not Peter, it was Satan talking to Christ through Peter, and Christ was literally talking to Satan. That is why Christ told Peter that Satan desired to sift him like wheat, and that he would pray for him that his faith would not fail.

Satan comes for all of us, the Deacon too. For some it is money, for some sex, for some hatred, but he comes at your weakness. So examine yourself: what is my weakness? Strengthen it, because that is where you will be tested and where Satan will try to destroy you. The worst are the ones who say they have no weakness, I’m perfect, I’m righteous: their demons are on another level, they are just good at hiding it. Everybody has weakness. Christ’s strength is made perfect in weakness. Paul fought his weakness and never gave in; he went to the Lord three times to take it away, and the Lord said no, fight it and become strong.

So just as Satan was working on Peter, Satan was there with Cain. The reason Cain’s countenance fell is that Satan did something to him right there, and the Lord saw it.

“And when the devil had ended all the temptation, he departed from him for a season.” Satan never stopped tempting Christ. He left only for a season and came back in different ways. When Christ was about to be crucified, Satan came back and jumped on Peter.

The war we are fighting cannot be seen; it is in the mind. Satan plays with your emotions, plays with people you care about, and puts thoughts in your mind that were not there, for you to go against God. That is how the root of bitterness destroys a lot of brothers.

“Ananias, why hath Satan filled thine heart to lie to the Holy Ghost”. That is what Satan does to us, and that is what happened with Cain.

This brother and sister sold their possession. If they wanted to keep back part for themselves they could have said so: we kept a little part, and this part we give to the school. But Satan told them to hide it and act like they were giving everything. The reason that thought came to their mind was Satan.

It is the same on your job. A co-worker comes by and a thought comes to your mind: damn, she got a fat ass. And you say, damn, why did I think that? Why did that thought come there? Or a sister on the job sees a dude: damn, he got muscles, he’s good looking. You ain’t said nothing, but the thought came. Satan whispered that; he plays on these things, and lust is the number one thing brothers deal with after bitterness. The war always starts in the mind; it does not start physically. You have to learn to control your thoughts. When evil thoughts come, it is not necessarily that you are evil and wicked; Satan plants them there. The question is whether you entertain it or shake it off: get behind me, Satan, as Christ said. Rebuke the thoughts in your mind. That is how you fight and win.

sense.text: “Let no man say when he is tempted, I am tempted of God: for God cannot be tempted with evil, neither tempteth he any man.” God doesn’t tempt you. Satan is the one tempting you. When wicked thoughts come to your mind, that is not God, that is Satan.

“But every man is tempted, when he is drawn away of his own lust, and enticed.” What does Satan tempt you with? Your own lust, the things you like. He draws you away with them. Your lust and your enticement are your weaknesses, the things you are fighting inside, and that is what he will try to get you with.

To understand this fight you have to put on the whole armor, and you have to examine yourself and know your weaknesses. Don’t ask anyone else what your weakness is. Figure it out and strengthen it, so Satan does not destroy you.

“Then when lust hath conceived”: where is lust conceived? In your mind. That is where the root begins.

You are going to see a woman. If you turn away, or learn to hate how she dresses, nothing is conceived. But if in your mind you say, I don’t mind sleeping with her, and you let that thought stay, then “it bringeth forth sin.” When the thought comes and you shake it off, it is not conceived: what’s wrong with you, God is going to kill you, stop thinking like that. You have to fight those thoughts. Adultery doesn’t start when you lie down with a woman; it starts in your mind.

“And sin, when it is finished, bringeth forth death.” After you do what you did, God is going to judge you. Some say, I committed adultery how many times, I fornicated how many times, and I did not die. That death is damnation. It is talking about your soul: you lose your soul.

precepts.why:
“Whosoever looketh on a woman to lust after her hath committed adultery with her already in his heart.” That is how lust is conceived.

We are living in an evil world and we all see beautiful women. When a picture of a woman was put up in front of the class, the brothers said it plainly: she is beautiful, but the way she dresses, you have to hate that thing, as Deacon Laban tells us. She has to dress modest. One older brother said he had been in the world a lot longer than in the truth, so he is still working on hating it.

What you see on that screen we are supposed to hate. But a lot of young men have not trained themselves to hate it yet; they see something like that walking down the street and break their neck. You see it every damn day when you go outside. You have to train yourself to hate evil, to train your mind; it doesn’t come naturally, and you don’t come to the truth and hate it all at once. When you see them, tell yourself: she got AIDS, it stinks, she is a man. It is a training thing. If you don’t do that, you will always be watching these things and desiring them. It also comes with age: the older brothers are more mature and say, she ain’t worth it.

Sisters too: before the truth many walked around in mini skirts and spandex, giggling and giving out their number. Now you come to the truth and say, I have to change the way I dress. When Christ returns there will be a modesty law set up.

sense.text:
Go back to Genesis: the root of bitterness jumped on Cain, and Satan was there whispering things in his ears and in his mind.

“For from within, out of the heart of men, proceed evil thoughts.” The thoughts you have, the things you hear in your mind: a lot of times that is Satan putting things there that are not there, not real, because Satan wants to defile you and put the root of bitterness inside of you. Out of the heart come “adulteries, fornications, murders”.
“Thefts, covetousness, wickedness, deceit, lasciviousness, an evil eye”: an evil eye is jealousy. “Blasphemy, pride, foolishness.”
“All these evil things come from within, and defile the man.” It comes from your mind. The root of bitterness comes from within, from your mind, and it forms a root and defiles you.

One point in the root of bitterness is correction. People become bitter a lot of times when they are corrected. “Correction is grievous unto him that forsaketh the way.”

Brothers develop bitterness, wives develop bitterness, because of correction. A brother gets corrected, and Satan enters his mind: they hate you, man, they never liked you, they ain’t right. And he listens to all those thoughts, which is Satan talking. It is like Wormtongue in The Lord of the Rings, whispering in the king’s ears. Wormtongue is Satan, or it could be the person next to you speaking evil in your ears.

Before bitterness becomes a root it must be a seed first: something has to be whispered in your mind. Once the seed starts growing into roots inside of you, you change, and you change for the worse. You may think nobody sees it, but everybody sees you have changed. You cannot hide bitterness.

Did Cain forsake the way? Yes. Was Cain corrected? Yes: the Lord told him, do well and you will be accepted. He did not want to listen, so correction was grievous to him. That is why he was angry and went and killed his brother. He became bitter against his brother.

That is one of the key things that make brothers lose the kingdom: they got corrected and became bitter. Some are corrected nicely, some get cussed out, and they get offended and say, I ain’t coming to the school no more. You have to be an idiot to leave the truth because a brother talked to you in a way you didn’t like. What can separate you from the love of God? Don’t let a harsh correction separate you from Christ.

“And he that hateth reproof shall die.” If you hate being corrected, if you don’t want nobody to tell you nothing, you are going to die.

Women do not like to be corrected, especially the American ones. Sisters, we love you, but many don’t want to take accountability: when they do wrong they won’t say, I’m sorry, and when their husband corrects them it has to be an argument and a fight with everything. Satan has done a job on our sisters. Accountability: that is their kryptonite. Many sisters, after being corrected by their husbands, became bitter against them and left the truth: ain’t no man ruling over me.

Husbands and wives will argue from time to time, and it is the husband’s job to correct her; that is part of ruling over her. Adam did not correct his wife. Satan deceived her and Adam went along with it, and that was his flaw: Eve was deceived, but he did it willingly. God told Adam, you better rule her; she don’t listen, you rule her. God commands us to rule over our wives, and to rule means to provide for her, to guide her, to correct her and teach her, as a man does for a woman he loves. It does not mean abuse, and it is not slavery and a man with a whip.

When a husband yells, it does not mean he hates you. Men lift their voice when they are angry. That week a sister called saying her husband was abusive; it was an argument. Some brothers slip with the tongue and say hurtful things they shouldn’t, but that is still not abuse. Abuse is abuse.

“And when Rachel saw that she bare Jacob no children, Rachel envied her sister”. Rachel was envious, and that envy is Satan: she thinks she’s all that with all them kids; I want babies too; I hate her. “And said unto Jacob, Give me children, or else I die.” Give me a baby or I’ll kill myself.

Rachel was very pretty; she was a dime, and that is why Jacob worked all those years for her. Very pretty women are often very manipulative, and they use their beauty to control and manipulate a man. Eve did that to Adam, and the same thing is being done to Jacob here: give me a baby or I’ll kill myself, I know you can’t live without me.

When a woman knows you love her more than God, she will try to use it against you. God took Ezekiel’s wife, the apple of his eye, and told him not to cry. Brothers, never put a woman above your God. Sisters, God comes first and you come after.

“And Jacob’s anger was kindled against Rachel: and he said, Am I in God’s stead”. Jacob was angry. You think he said it softly? He said it with a lifted voice: woman, what the hell do I look like? Am I God, woman? What the hell you talking about, you going to kill yourself? So go kill yourself then. Moses saw the whole argument and wrote it down in a kosher way for us; Jacob may have flipped the table over.

“Who hath withheld from thee the fruit of the womb?” Is God why you ain’t getting pregnant? Because of the evil you do: Jacob knew she was still worshipping idols.

So when a man gets angry he lifts his voice and he yells, and that is not abuse. He is correcting you. Take the correction, see what he is saying and fix it; don’t justify yourself. When a woman justifies herself she becomes bitter: in her mind, he was wrong for what he said to me, and Satan says, yeah, that’s abuse. And you listening to Satan with your dumb stupid behind. Now you are divorced with three, four kids, and no other man wants you. Now you left your husband.

Brothers, rule over your wives, and to rule over her means to love her. If you love a woman you are going to correct her, and she will become better. Not abuse.
